issues.legal_issue: A delayed challenge to an acquisition notification for insufficiently particularized public purpose is barred when the challenger did not raise the alleged prejudice at the appropriate stage.
material_facts: The notification covered a large area comprising plots belonging to different persons and specified the purpose as the planned development of the city.
A declaration covering part of the area was published in 1966, but the challengers waited until 1970 or later to contest the notification.
The challengers did not argue before the High Court that insufficient particulars had prevented them from effectively objecting to the acquisition.
issues.conclusion: The Court declined to consider the challenge, holding that the challengers’ delay and failure to raise the alleged prejudice earlier barred it.
issues.legal_principle: A valid notification under section 4 of the Land Acquisition Act is a sine qua non for acquisition proceedings, and the particular public purpose must be specified sufficiently to allow meaningful objections under sections 4(2) and 5A. For a large acquisition involving many plots, the purpose may be specified with reference to the area as a whole; whether the specification is sufficient depends on the circumstances. A challenge brought after delay, particularly after the challenger has allowed proceedings to advance and did not raise the asserted prejudice below, may be rejected for laches and acquiescence. The Court relied on Munshi Singh v. Union of India, Arnold Rodricks v. State of Maharashtra, Tilokchand Motichand v. H. B. Munshi, and Rabindranath Bose v. Union of India.

rule.if: acquisition_notification_challenge and large_area_multiple_owners and challenge_delayed_after_declaration and alleged_objection_prejudice_not_raised_below

predicates.acquisition_notification_challenge: A person challenges the validity of a notification initiating compulsory acquisition proceedings.
predicates.large_area_multiple_owners: The acquisition covers a large area made up of plots belonging to multiple owners.
predicates.challenge_delayed_after_declaration: The challenger waits until after a formal declaration advancing the acquisition before challenging the notification.
predicates.alleged_objection_prejudice_not_raised_b: The challenger does not raise before the lower court the claim that the notification prevented an effective objection.

issues.definition: When a challenger to an acquisition notification waits until after the acquisition has advanced and did not earlier raise the claimed prejudice, the challenge is barred by laches.

issues.legal_issue: Delay in completing acquisition proceedings does not invalidate the acquisition when the delay is explained by the processing of numerous objections and pending challenges to the proceedings.
material_facts: Approximately 6,000 objections were filed by interested persons.
Several petitions challenging the acquisition proceedings were filed in 1966 and 1967.
The Government waited for the objections and petitions to be dealt with before proceeding further.
issues.conclusion: The Court agreed that the Government had not caused inordinate delay in completing the acquisition proceedings.
issues.legal_principle: Whether delay in completing acquisition proceedings is inordinate depends on the circumstances. The Court accepted that the Government necessarily had to wait for numerous objections and pending petitions to be disposed of, and saw no basis to depart from the High Court’s assessment.

rule.if: acquisition_proceeding and numerous_objections_pending and acquisition_challenges_pending and government_waited_for_disposal

predicates.acquisition_proceeding: The proceeding concerns compulsory acquisition of land.
predicates.numerous_objections_pending: A large number of interested persons have filed objections that remain to be dealt with.
predicates.acquisition_challenges_pending: Court challenges to the acquisition proceedings remain pending.
predicates.government_waited_for_disposal: The Government delayed further steps while the objections and court challenges were being dealt with.

issues.definition: In an acquisition proceeding, when numerous objections and court challenges are pending and the Government waits for their disposal, its resulting delay is not inordinate.

issues.legal_issue: A challenge to the statutory date used to determine compensation cannot succeed merely because the claimant considers the resulting compensation inadequate, and a provision that does not regulate procedure cannot be invalidated for procedural unreasonableness.
material_facts: The claimants objected that compensation was calculated by reference to market value on the date of the acquisition notification rather than the later date when possession would be taken.
The Land Acquisition Act was enacted before the Constitution.
The challenge concerned the amount of compensation produced by the valuation date, not a procedure for determining compensation that denied the owner a hearing.
issues.conclusion: The Court rejected the challenge, holding that the adequacy of compensation was not open to challenge on that basis and that the compensation provision did not regulate procedure in a way that could be procedurally unreasonable.
issues.legal_principle: Article 31(5)(a) protects an existing law from challenge under Article 31(2), and a complaint that the compensation calculated under section 23 of the Land Acquisition Act is inadequate is, in substance, a challenge to adequacy of compensation. Under R. C. Cooper v. Union of India, a challenge under Article 19(1)(f) to a law for compulsory acquisition would ordinarily concern procedural reasonableness; a provision fixing the valuation basis, rather than procedure, cannot be challenged for procedural unreasonableness.

rule.if: compulsory_acquisition_compensation_challenge and pre_constitution_acquisition_law and objection_based_on_valuation_date and no_procedural_defect_alleged

predicates.compulsory_acquisition_compensation_chal: The proceeding challenges the compensation basis used in a compulsory acquisition.
predicates.pre_constitution_acquisition_law: The law governing the acquisition existed before the Constitution came into force.
predicates.objection_based_on_valuation_date: The claimant objects that compensation is measured using an earlier valuation date and is therefore inadequate.
predicates.no_procedural_defect_alleged: The challenge does not identify a defect in the procedure for determining compensation.

issues.definition: When a challenge to compensation under a pre-existing acquisition law rests on the valuation date and alleges no procedural defect, the compensation basis is not invalidated for inadequacy.

issues.legal_issue: Land may be acquired for planned development before development plans are ready or the land has been declared a development area.
material_facts: The Government had decided on planned development before the relevant development statute came into force.
The acquisition notification was issued before a master plan was ready and before the area had been declared a development area.
The challenge concerned acquisition for planned development, rather than the lawfulness of carrying out development without the required approval or sanction.
issues.conclusion: The Court held that the absence of a master plan or development-area declaration did not prevent acquisition of land for planned development.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 12 and 15 of the Delhi Development Act address different matters: section 12 regulates development, while section 15 provides for acquisition of land required for development or another purpose under that Act. Acquisition may precede development. Land may be acquired for planned development before a master plan is ready, although subsequent development must comply with the applicable requirements, including obtaining the relevant approval or sanction. The Court relied on Patna Improvement Trust v. Smt. Lakshmi Devi.

predicates.acquisition_proceeding: The proceeding concerns compulsory acquisition of land.
predicates.purpose_is_planned_development: The land is acquired for a program of planned development.
predicates.development_plan_not_ready: The relevant development plan has not yet been prepared when the land is acquired.

issues.definition: When land is acquired for planned development before the relevant plan is ready, the acquisition may proceed before that plan exists.

issues.legal_issue: A delayed challenge to the authority that issued an acquisition notification may be rejected for laches and acquiescence without deciding whether that authority was authorized to issue it.
material_facts: The acquisition notification was issued by a local administrative officer, while the challengers contended that the development statute assigned the acquisition power to the Central Government.
The challengers did not timely challenge the notification and allowed the acquisition proceedings to advance.
The Court assumed, without deciding, that the officer might not have been authorized and rejected the challenge because of laches and acquiescence.
issues.conclusion: The Court rejected the challenge to the issuing officer’s authority because the challengers were precluded by laches and acquiescence from questioning the notification.
issues.legal_principle: A challenge to the authority responsible for issuing an acquisition notification relates primarily to the validity of that notification. Where the challenger is precluded by laches and acquiescence from questioning the notification, the challenge may be rejected without resolving whether the authority was in fact authorized. Section 15 of the Delhi Development Act was the asserted source of the claimed allocation of power.

predicates.acquisition_notification_challenge: A person challenges the validity of a notification initiating compulsory acquisition proceedings.
predicates.authority_to_issue_disputed: The challenger claims that the official who issued the notification lacked authority to do so.
predicates.challenge_delayed_after_proceedings_adva: The challenger waits until acquisition proceedings have advanced before contesting the issuing official’s authority.

issues.definition: When a challenger disputes the issuing official’s authority only after acquisition proceedings have advanced, the authority challenge may be barred by laches.

issues.legal_issue: The later allotment of acquired land to cooperative housing societies does not, by itself, make an acquisition one for a company or attract the statutory procedure for company acquisitions.
material_facts: The stated purpose of the acquisition was planned development.
After acquisition, the Government proposed to allot, or allotted, a portion of the land to cooperative housing societies for development.
The Court was not satisfied that the societies had provided the funds for the acquisition.
issues.conclusion: The Court held that the acquisition was not shown to be for a company and that the later allotment did not attract Part VII of the Land Acquisition Act.
issues.legal_principle: The character of an acquisition is determined by its purpose, not merely by a later transfer or allotment of part of the acquired property to a cooperative housing society. Later allotment does not make the acquisition one for a company, and Part VII of the Land Acquisition Act is not attracted on that basis alone. The Court also found no sufficient basis to conclude that the cooperative societies provided the acquisition funds.

rule.if: company_acquisition_procedure_challenge and acquisition_for_public_development and land_later_allotted_to_cooperative_societies and society_funding_not_established

predicates.company_acquisition_procedure_challenge: A challenger argues that special statutory procedures for acquisitions for companies should have been followed.
predicates.acquisition_for_public_development: The acquisition was made for a public development purpose.
predicates.land_later_allotted_to_cooperative_socie: After acquisition, the Government proposes to or does allot part of the land to cooperative housing societies.
predicates.society_funding_not_established: The evidence does not establish that the societies provided the funds for the acquisition.

issues.definition: When land is acquired for public development and later allotted partly to cooperative societies, without establishing that they funded the acquisition, the company-acquisition procedure is not required.
